newsitem.title: USA: CPUC adopts plan to speed electric restructuring.
newsitem.headline: CPUC adopts plan to speed electric restructuring.

text.p: The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) on Friday adopted a revised plan to expedite restructuring of the state's electric utility industry which takes into account a new state law.
Legislation passed in Calfornia earlier this year stipulates phasing-in of open competition between electricity providers beginning January 1, 1998.
The commission also halted preparations for an environmental review of the restructuring plan, saying that the state legislation takes precedence in planning the new market.
The CPUC said it will establish an annual revenue adjustment proceeding to keep track of utilities authorized and actual revenue requirements.
The commission also plans to work closely with federal regulators and other states to ensure reliability of the electric system.
The new plan also calls for adoption of direct-access tariffs by October 1997 and for the commission to make a final decision on utilities' transition costs by October 22, 1997.
The CPUC will hold hearings and make a final decision on transfer of transmission facilities in the state to an independent system operator late next year.
